checked_sources.source: Zirui Cao et al., A Budget-Adaptive Allocation Rule for Optimal Computing Budget Allocation, European Journal of Operational Research 325(2), 2025; arXiv:2304.02377v4
checked_sources.result: Recovered exact finite-budget PCS tables and the practical sequential rules. The paper defines inverse signal-to-noise I_i = sigma_i^2/delta_i,b^2, asymptotic OCBA weights proportional to I_i, a finite-budget regime T=O(k log k), and an asymptotic regime T=omega(k log k). FAA/DAA use plug-in current sample means/variances and a budget-adaptive correction; DAA recomputes against t+1 and does not require a known final budget.

checked_sources.source: Roger Kober et al., Sequential experimental designs for discrimination among adsorption equilibrium models, Chemical Engineering Research and Design 170, 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.cherd.2021.04.025
checked_sources.type: primary journal article/abstract and article metadata
checked_sources.result: Real dye-adsorption experiments on tartrazine/MgO and methyl-orange/activated-carbon. The sequential design chooses controllable experimental conditions to discriminate rival adsorption-isotherm models while updating posterior uncertainty. For methyl orange, discrimination was achieved only after five additional experiments; the method can also indicate when discrimination may not be attainable and can trigger model-set revision.

checked_sources.source: Dual MPC for Active Learning of Nonparametric Uncertainties, European Journal of Control, online 30 July 2026; arXiv version
checked_sources.result: In the reported mass-spring-damper numerical study, passive dual GP-MPC achieved 0.17% and 0.13% steady-state error at 5 s and 10 s, while the proposed active dual GP-MPC achieved 0.19% and 0.13%, with average solve time 0.295 s. The paper leaves deeper active-versus-passive performance analysis to future work. This is not the sought physical plant/robot matched-benefit experiment and does not show an unconditional active-exploration advantage.

checked_sources.source: K. Heirung, B. Foss, B. Ydstie, MPC-based dual control with online experiment design, Journal of Process Control, 2015
checked_sources.result: Supports online experiment-design/dual-control mechanisms that trade control and information acquisition and reports improved simulated control performance with reduced output variance/control effort, but the accessible evidence checked in this run did not provide the required matched physical-plant identification-speed plus closed-loop-cost result.

candidates_new.mechanism: Allocate evaluation budget using estimated gap-to-best and variance, with a finite-budget correction that deliberately avoids over-concentrating on hard-to-distinguish candidates when evidence is scarce; continuously relax toward asymptotic OCBA as budget/evidence grows. Prefer a dynamic rule such as DAA when the final evaluation budget is not known in advance.
candidates_new.primary_source: Cao et al., A Budget-Adaptive Allocation Rule for Optimal Computing Budget Allocation, EJOR 2025 / arXiv:2304.02377v4
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Exact primary PCS tables show consistent finite-budget gains over classical OCBA. Example 1: at T=400, DAA 0.886 versus OCBA 0.856 (+3.0 percentage points); at T=1000, 0.969 versus 0.950 (+1.9 pp). Example 3: at T=1000, 0.822 versus 0.762 (+6.0 pp), and at T=2000, 0.920 versus 0.864 (+5.6 pp). Example 4: at T=6000, 0.690 versus 0.613 (+7.7 pp); at T=20000, 0.870 versus 0.746 (+12.4 pp); at T=40000, 0.907 versus 0.785 (+12.2 pp). Facility-location example: at T=120, 0.743 versus 0.715 (+2.8 pp), and at T=300, 0.889 versus 0.863 (+2.6 pp). Large-scale Example 5 gains were smaller but positive: 0.722 versus 0.706 at 600k and 0.907 versus 0.892 at 1.2m. Runtime overhead remained the same broad order as OCBA in the paper's tables, though typically around 2x for the lightweight allocation computation; in simulation-dominated facility-location cases wall-clock differences were small relative to simulation cost.
candidates_new.operational_observable: Estimate current best b, sample means, sample variances, and per-candidate inverse SNR I_i_hat = s_i^2/(mean_i-mean_b)^2. Use the paper's plug-in finite-budget threshold/correction rather than a fixed time-only switch. DAA's next-sample rule is based on the largest allocation deficit relative to the dynamically recomputed target weights at t+1. A simplified scheduler can treat unstable/small gaps and remaining budget near O(k log k) as a signal to stay broad, only becoming OCBA-like as evidence and budget grow.
candidates_new.scope: Normal-sampling ranking-and-selection assumptions and tested numerical/simulation examples. Gains are not universal percentages; the largest reported differences occur in specific examples. Dynamic feedback between allocation and estimation is still an approximation rather than exact finite-horizon dynamic programming.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For expensive research candidate evaluation, avoid equal allocation and avoid premature winner-take-most allocation. Re-estimate difficulty from observed variance and performance gaps each evaluation step, allocate the next trial to the largest evidence deficit, and increase concentration only when the budget/evidence regime supports it.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source-domain result; medium-high for transferable scheduler principle

candidates_new.mechanism: Choose each next experiment to maximally separate currently plausible rival mechanistic models, update model probabilities/parameter uncertainty after each result, permit model-set revision when all current models fit poorly, and explicitly stop when available interventions cannot discriminate the remaining models.
candidates_new.primary_source: Kober et al., Sequential experimental designs for discrimination among adsorption equilibrium models, Chemical Engineering Research and Design 170 (2021), DOI 10.1016/j.cherd.2021.04.025
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: The method was applied to real adsorption experiments rather than only simulation. For methyl-orange adsorption on activated carbon, the paper reports that model discrimination was achieved only after five additional sequentially selected experiments. For tartrazine/MgO, new information caused re-evaluation of the model set and inclusion of models not considered initially. Both cases selected the BET isotherm.
candidates_new.scope: The accessible primary abstract establishes five additional experiments and real laboratory application, but this run did not recover a matched random-design experiment count or full numerical uncertainty trajectory from the paywalled full text. Therefore do not convert the five experiments into a speedup factor versus a baseline.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: When several explanations remain plausible, schedule tests for expected discrimination among the live hypotheses rather than generic uncertainty reduction. Preserve an explicit 'none of the current hypotheses is adequate / cannot discriminate with available actions' state so the system revises the model set instead of forcing a winner.
candidates_new.confidence: high for real experimental feasibility and reported five-step result; medium for sample-efficiency magnitude versus alternative designs

evidence_updates.update: The previously unresolved exact finite-budget magnitude is now recovered from Cao et al.'s primary PCS tables. The practical guardrail should be implemented as continuous budget-adaptive weighting from current gaps/variances (especially DAA when total budget is unknown), not merely a hard global T threshold. The strongest extracted example-level DAA-vs-OCBA gains range from about +1.5 to +12.4 PCS percentage points across the tested tables, with exact scope retained per example.

A 2026 active dual GP-MPC numerical study does not provide evidence that explicit active exploration is always superior: reported steady-state errors were essentially tied with passive dual GP-MPC (0.19% vs 0.17% at 5 s; both 0.13% at 10 s). Treat exploration as information-value-gated rather than mandatory.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: In the checked 2026 dual GP-MPC study, active and passive approaches were essentially tied on reported steady-state error, with active 0.19% versus passive 0.17% at 5 s and both 0.13% at 10 s.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Reject 'always probe' as a default. Explicit exploration should be triggered only when expected discrimination/information value exceeds control/task cost and when passive task trajectories are insufficiently informative.
